newsitem.title: USA: Health Risk may still benefit as merger collapses.
newsitem.headline: Health Risk may still benefit as merger collapses.

text.p: Health Risk Management Inc may still benefit from a continuing relationship with HealthPlan Services Corp, in spite of the collapse of their proposed merger, industry analysts said Thursday.

"Health Risk may come out of this ahead," Ted Levy, an analyst at Essex Capital Markets Inc, said. "The deal was a great fit, but it seems the continuing relationship suggests future benefits for Health Risk since HealthPlan needs Health Risk's products."
The companies terminated the $80-million deal Thursday.

Health Risk, which provides health care management products, and HealthPlan, which offers health care management services, both cited an unwillingness to close a deal that would be of less value and dilutive in the near term.
Instead, HealthPlan agreed to buy 200,000 Health Risk shares, representing about 4.5 percent of the company's stock, and keep in place a joint marketing pact signed in September.

The companies said the deal, originally set to close in early 1997, was also derailed by a lengthy review by the Securities and Exchange Commission that one analyst said took two and a half months to complete.
"(The collapse) was bad news for Health Risk, but not a disaster," Mark Kelliher, an analyst at Principal Financial Securities, said.
"HealthPlan couldn't fold Health Risk into its operations without suffering some sort of dilution," Kelliher said.
Kelliher also said the stock purchase by HealthPlan is significant in that it will continue their relationship.
Both Kelliher and Levy said the pressure of dilution of HealthPlan stock made the companies decide to pull the plug.
Levy and Kelliher also both said it is possible the two sides could return to the bargaining table.
"They may want to revive the deal if the shares come back," Levy said.
Kelliher was less optimistic, saying "it would take surprisingly powerful, strong quarterly results by Health Risk in the March and June quarters to convince HealthPlan to come back to the aisle."
Bob Hoehn, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, echoed that sentiment.
"They may revisit this deal in the future," he said. "But HealthPlan has enough opportunities with the other acquisitions it made last year."
"HealthPlan probably looked at this (deal) and said we already have a lot on our plate, and they do," Hoehn said.
HealthPlan shares were off 7/8 Thursday at 16-3/4, while Health Risk stock was down 2-15/16 at 10-1/16.
